newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's JGC Corp says profits plunge.
newsitem.headline: Japan's JGC Corp says profits plunge.

text.p: Japanese plant engineering company JGC Corp on Tuesday announced a nearly 70 percent plunge in its half-year earnings, which it attributed to excessive competition and delays in finishing overseas projects.

JGC, whose projects include petroleum, chemical, electric power and gas plants, announced a parent current profit of 834 million yen in the six months to September 30, down 67.5 percent from the same period a year earlier.
The company said it would plunge into the red for the full year, with a parent current loss of 9.5 billion yen after profits of 6.49 billion yen the year before.
"Looking at plant orders, capital investment by our domestic clients, such as oil refining and petrochemical companies, remains stagnant," the company said in a statement.
"Such investment in overseas markets is active...but the scale is getting smaller. We are also facing severe competition with our rivals there," it added.

For the full year, the company expects to receive plant orders worth about 300 billion yen, unchanged from an estimate made earlier this year. But falling profitability in some plants and delays in finishing projects forced the company to revise down its business prospects for the year.
